title: Preemptive Prefill Pacekeeper & Cross-SKU Kernel Arbitrator
creator: Asha Patel
description: Objective: Implement a runtime component (Prefill Pacekeeper) that proactively paces prefill/concurrent decode starts across mixed-SKU MIG partitions and full GPUs, and a complementary Cross-SKU Kernel Arbitrator that ranks kernel candidates by latency/cost under current clock/thermal headroom. The goal is to reduce prefill-triggered clock thrash and tail latency spikes (p95/p99) on shared MIG fleets while preserving throughput for steady-state decode. This ticket covers design, implementation, microbench validation, and canary rollout to a dedicated hetero-sku pool.
background: We observed recurrent p99 latency spikes during bursty prefill workloads when mixed H100/L40S/A10 devices are co-located and MIG partitions hit thermal/clipped clock states. Current kernel selection picks the fastest kernel offline, but it does not account for transient clock headroom or immediate thermal projection. Prefill bursts start many kernels simultaneously, causing clock governors to oscillate and NVLink saturation in multi-GPU pods. This increases token latency and reduces overall throughput. Existing work touches clock steering and kernel hints, but we need a run-time pacing + arbitration layer that uses live telemetry to avoid thrash.
technical_details: Prefill Pacekeeper component: token-aware admission control for prefill windows. Uses sequence-length estimate, customer QoS tier, and recent clock/thermal headroom to stagger prefill starts into soft micro-batches (20-200ms windows), preventing large concurrent kernel wakeups.

Cross-SKU Kernel Arbitrator: compute a kernel_score for each candidate kernel: kernel_score = latency_est * (1 + clock_penalty + nvlink_penalty + thermal_penalty) / throughput_est. clock_penalty is derived from predicted clock rollback probability over next 5s from recent telemetry.

Telemetry inputs: per-slice clock (MHz), thermal headroom (degC margin to throttling), power draw, GPU util, NVLink TX/RX, recent kernel latency histogram (p50/p95/p99), and token density distribution for incoming requests.

Control loop: lightweight predictive filter (exponential smoothing) + conservative PID terms to adjust admission rate. Decision frequency = 100ms. Adjustable safety_factor per release and customer tier.

Prefill scheduling changes: when safety_factor > threshold, convert immediate prefill into serialized warmups: first wave warms KV cache and memory maps using low-precision kernels (quantized probe), then escalate to production kernel if headroom remains.

Fallbacks: if thermal projection indicates imminent throttling, prefer quantized kernels with lower memory bandwidth; if NVLink > 80% saturation, prefer kernels that minimize inter-GPU transfers (local microbatching).

Implementation touches: runtime scheduler, kernel registry adapter (to expose kernel_score hooks), telemetry ingestion (extend existing metrics/feature flags), and unit/integration tests for deterministic simulation harness.

Performance targets: reduce p99 prefill latency by >= 30% for mixed-sku workloads in our staging fleet while keeping p50 within 10% of baseline and throughput degradation <= 8% for steady-state traffic.
Compatibility: must be opt-in per deployment via runtime config; default disabled for legacy clusters until canary validated.
Safety: add an override to force immediate prefill for high-priority enterprise customers; record audit logs for all pacing decisions.
Testing: synthetic bursts (sequence lengths 8/64/1024) across H100/L40S/A10 MIG mixes; thermal soak runs for 30 minutes to validate steady-state behavior.
APIs: expose judge metrics in Console (route-level prefill-delay histograms, pace decisions, kernel_choice counts) and add rollout toggles (canary fraction, safety_factor).
acceptance_criteria: Prefill Pacekeeper merged with feature flag runtime.prefill_pacekeeper and default off
Cross-SKU Kernel Arbitrator integrated with kernel registry and used by prefill path when enabled
End-to-end microbench shows >=30% reduction in p99 prefill latency on hetero-sku staging cluster (report attached)
Console dashboard updated with prefill pacing metrics and canary toggle
Automated integration test that simulates a mixed-sku burst and verifies no regression in throughput > -8%
Design doc and rollout plan reviewed by Runtime and Infra leads
Customer-impact statement and enterprise override implemented
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag; 2) Run synthetic validation on isolated hetero-sku staging pool; 3) Canary to 5% of dedicated runtime-hetero clusters for 72h with alert thresholds; 4) Expand to 25% for 7d if no regressions; 5) Full enable for dedicated pools and opt-in for hosted customers. Rollback plan: toggle off feature flag; auto-fallback to previous kernel selection path.
telemetry_queries: dashboard:prefill.p99_by_cluster_shard - time-series of prefill p99 over last 7d
metric_query: SELECT percentile(99, kernel_latency_ms) FROM kernel_exec WHERE cluster='staging-hetero' AND window=5m
alert_query: avg(nvlink_tx_bytes_s) > 80% AND avg(prefill_concurrent_warmups) > 10 => fire throttling-warning

notes_for_reviewer: Key review areas: correctness of kernel_score formula under real telemetry jitter, safety of admission control (no deadlocks or request starvation), and observability coverage. Please validate acceptance queries and canary thresholds.
